Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: Known asthma with atopic background; ran out of inhalers for ~1 week; recent viral URI; now with 3 hours of chest tightness, wheeze, non-productive cough, and mild exertional dyspnea without rest dyspnea or chest pain.
- Differential diagnoses (aligned with DDx):
  - Acute asthma exacerbation (likely viral-triggered; worsened by lapse in inhaled corticosteroid and SABA) – highly consistent with transcript.
  - Post-viral bronchial hyperreactivity contributing to cough and wheeze – plausible and may overlap with asthma.
  - Other causes (pneumonia, PE, spontaneous pneumothorax) considered low likelihood in DDx and not supported by transcript features.
- Working diagnosis: Acute asthma exacerbation (viral-triggered), with loss of control due to lapse in controller/reliever medications.
- Management priorities: Resume controller (ICS) and reliever (SABA); short course of oral steroids; spacer use; safety-netting for deterioration; rest.

Management Plan

- Medications prescribed:
  - Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler PRN for wheeze/shortness of breath (dose/frequency not documented).
  - Beclomethasone (Clenil Modulite) inhaler for maintenance once improved (dose/frequency not documented).
  - Oral steroid tablets for 5 days, 2 tablets each morning (drug name and strength not documented).
  - Spacer device supplied; instructions provided.
- Self-care and education:
  - Use spacer with inhaler as instructed (prime; inhale via spacer for approximately 5–10 breaths per dose).
  - Use beclomethasone daily as controller once acute symptoms stabilize; use salbutamol as needed.
  - If needing salbutamol more often than every 3 hours, seek medical attention.
  - Seek urgent care for worsening shortness of breath, increasing chest tightness, light-headedness, or other concerning symptoms.
  - Rest; time off work advised (self-certify for up to 7 days).
- Follow-up: Formal follow-up appointment not recorded; advised to seek medical attention if symptoms worsen.
- Investigations/referrals: None recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Acute asthma exacerbation (High): Known asthma; week-long lapse in ICS/SABA; recent URI; wheeze, chest tightness, exertional dyspnea; prior severe exacerbation history.
- Post-viral bronchial hyperreactivity/acute viral bronchitis (Moderate): Recent cold with persistent non-productive cough and mild wheeze; may overlap with asthma.
- Community-acquired pneumonia (Low): Cough and dyspnea present, but no fever, sputum, pleuritic pain, or focal findings recorded.

Quality checks

- Missing expected elements: Vital signs (including oxygen saturation), peak flow or spirometry, physical examination findings, BMI/anthropometrics, immunization review, smoking/alcohol/substance history, mental health screening, hearing/vision screening, urinalysis, STI risk/screening, preventive care review (e.g., influenza vaccine), documented asthma action plan and medication dosing.
- Internal contradictions: None noted between transcript and DDx.
- Transcript quality: Telehealth consultation without objective measurements; brief audio dropouts reported; overall clinical details adequate for acute management but incomplete for comprehensive health assessment.
